text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
MakesPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
InvitesCeremony(x) ::: x invites others to come to their ceremony.
WellAttended(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
InvitesFriends(x) ::: x invites friends to their ceremony.
Premises:
∀x (MakesPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are people who are engaged.
∀x (InvitesCeremony(x) → MakesPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others to come to their ceremony make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttended(x) → InvitesCeremony(x)) ::: Anyone who has a well-attended wedding invites others to come to their ceremony.
∃x (WellAttended(x) ∧ LargerFamily(x)) ::: Some people that have well-attended weddings have larger families.
Engaged(john) → ¬(InvitesFriends(john) ∨ MakesPlans(john)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends to their ceremony and make wedding plans.
LargerFamily(john) → (WellAttended(john) ∨ InvitesFriends(john)) ::: If John has a larger family, then either John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends to their ceremony.
Conclusion:
¬(LargerFamily(john) ∨ InvitesCeremony(john)) ::: John neither has a larger family nor does he invite others to his wedding.
